title: Graystone Ballroom: Hampton, Hines and Coleman Hawkins
summary: The Graystone Ballroom bands, Hampton's first band, outings with Aunt Lydia to hear Earl Hines, and Hawkins's 'Body and Soul'.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: And there was a ballroom there called the Graystone Ballroom, where the big bands used to play -- a big, fancy

ballroom up on Woodward Avenue. The Paradise Theatre was also on Woodward Avenue. And I heard a lot of great bands there. That's where I first heard Lionel Hampton's band when he first came on tour with his band, the first band, when he had Illinois Jacquet and Dexter Gordon, and Marshall Royal and Ernie Royal, Karl George was one of the trumpet players -- he had some band!

But one of my favorites was Earl Fatha Hines. My Aunt Lydia... We used to go to dances together all the time, because my uncle, he didn't care anything about that, you know. We'd always go. And her favorite saxophone player was Budd Johnson. And whenever Earl Hines came down, she'd say, 'Let's go hear Mister Johnson.' They came out with that record, 'Please, Mister Johnson'... Ha-ha, that was something beautiful, you know, to see Eckstine and Madeleine Green and all those people, you know.

It was really a treat to have these outlets where you could go and hear people. It just opened you up so much, you know. Coleman Hawkins came through there after he came from Europe; he played the Graystone Ballroom. And 'Body and Soul' was on all the jukeboxes. You know, his classic; it was on all of the jukeboxes. It was really something special.
No. I hadn't ever even picked up a tenor saxophone. I was still playing my alto and my clarinet.
No, nothing at all. No. Alto was it. [LAUGHS] Yeah...
